Keep the surrounding blank wall.
2. Replace the framed repeated botanical picture above the distant dining sideboard with ONE original square textile artwork: abstract folded ivory petals and just a thin muted wine thread, in a thin walnut shadow frame. This is a different medium and composition from the plaster.
3. Keep the small dining round table and mix of light upholstered / cane-backed chairs. Replace its globe pendant with one airy handwoven bamboo petal pendant, three overlapping thin softly curved leaf/petal shells, warm ivory diffusor inside, sculptural but modest and hung only over the dining table. The main living ceiling fitting stays understated.
4. Keep the olive sofa, pale small scalloped stone coffee table, thin brass legs and slim honey-walnut TV cabinet. Refine two cabinet fronts with fine tightly woven cane inset behind a clear protective surface; retain one small oxblood panel. Change the floral-printed cushion to a plain cream pillow with an original raised stitched organic petal contour. Retain one wine accent cushion.
5. REMOVE all the repeated round beige vases with berry bouquets, including TV console, table, side table and dining sideboard. ONLY ONE small ikebana of two white calla lilies in a low dark oxblood glazed asymmetric bowl on the coffee table, arranged low so it doesn't block the room. Dining table has only a shallow hand-formed ceramic bowl with three pears; dining sideboard has one empty sculptural blue-green glass vessel and a small lamp. TV console has a closed book and one small bronze object. Preserve generous empty tabletops.
Make the plaster relief and woven pendant clearly legible while preserving the original photographic realism and intimate scale.
